Stop emulating. Start executing natively. 🚀

Running Nintendo Switch games on Apple Silicon usually means heavy CPU emulation overhead, thermal throttling, and drained batteries. S2Arm completely changes the game by bridging the architecture gap through ahead-of-time (AOT) static binary translation and direct graphics mapping.

Instead of translating instructions at runtime, S2Arm rewrites Switch game binaries directly into native ARM64 at build time for raw processor execution. Combined with a direct Metal graphics pipeline, it translates API calls straight to Apple Metal for high framerates, low heat, and optimal efficiency. 

Plus, for the automation nerds and AI engineers: it features AI-driven operations via a control interface (s2armctl) that lets AI assistants programmatically manage builds, imports, and diagnostics. It even packages your entire game library into a single app slot to bypass multi-app limitations on iOS, iPadOS, and macOS.

If you are a systems engineer, emulation developer, or toolchain architect interested in cross-architecture compilation, this is a must-study codebase.

Explore the source code and start building today:
https://github.com/jhaizhou-ops/S2Arm

Tired of mysterious OOM errors while running local LLMs and AI workloads? Meet gputaskman: an htop for your GPU that finally reveals what is actually consuming your VRAM—from model weights to KV caches—across Windows, Linux, WSL, and macOS.

Traditional GPU monitors like Task Manager or nvidia-smi only show aggregate VRAM consumption, leaving developers completely blind to specific processes, model files, and memory buffers. 

gputaskman bridges this gap with a powerful terminal UI that connects per-process GPU memory and engine activity directly to your loaded runtimes, model files, and buffer breakdowns.

Key Features:
- Per-process VRAM and engine activity tracking across Windows (WDDM), Linux (NVML and amdgpu drm-fdinfo), WSL, and macOS Apple Silicon.
- Granular LLM breakdown separating model weights, compute buffers, and KV-cache allocations.
- Container-aware process mapping for Docker and Kubernetes environments where host PIDs do not align with container namespaces.
- Cross-platform portable execution with zero-dependency installations via uv, pipx, or standalone binaries.

Whether you are debugging memory leaks during local LLM inference and fine-tuning with Ollama, llama.cpp, or PyTorch, or monitoring multi-container GPU allocations on rented GPU boxes, gputaskman gives you instant hardware observability right from your terminal.

Check out the repo and drop a star if it saves your workflows:
https://github.com/shanselman/gputaskman

🤖 Giving AI agents free rein on your phone sounds great until they accidentally wipe your data or make an unauthorized transfer. 

How do we let LLMs automate mobile workflows without risking our security?

Meet Pinky: an innovative open-source framework and native app that bridges the gap between conversational AI agents and mobile device automation by introducing human-in-the-loop oversight directly at the gateway layer. 📱✨

🔍 The Problem:
Building and testing agentic workflows that interact with physical or emulated mobile devices is terrifying. Uncontrolled AI agents can execute dangerous actions, touch sensitive apps, or bypass safety rules when talking users into self-approval. 

⚡ The Solution:
Pinky solves this by intercepting actions at the Model Context Protocol (MCP) gateway level. Any MCP-compatible agent—like Claude Code, Cursor, or your own custom scripts—can interact with Android and iOS devices, but critical, risky, or out-of-scope actions are forced to wait for explicit human approval.

🚀 Key Features:
• Gateway-Enforced Approvals: Security rules and human sign-offs run directly inside the gateway layer, so agents cannot bypass restrictions.
• Off-Limits App Protection: Banking apps, password managers, and crypto wallets are invisible to agents by default, blocking unauthorized interactions with OTP and password fields.
• Native Desktop Client: Built with MyGo for direct GPU rendering (no Electron!), making it a lightweight multi-platform client for macOS, Windows, and Linux with super low resource usage.
• Universal Support: Integrates with any MCP-compatible agent and drives Android (10-17) and iOS (17.4+) on both physical devices and emulators.

Whether you are building automated mobile regression testing suites with LLM agents or setting up secure personal assistant workflows, Pinky provides the exact security abstraction layer developers need.

👉 Check out the repository and secure your mobile AI workflows today:
https://github.com/DIYgod/pinky

Run native macOS directly on your iPhone and iPad? That is no longer just a sci-fi dream. 🍎📱

Meet Henge: an engineering marvel that emulates full macOS arm64 directly on iOS and iPadOS devices using a custom JIT, MMU, and Metal-accelerated virtual GPU. No QEMU. No Virtualization.framework. 

💡 The Problem Solved:
iOS apps lack a native hypervisor layer, making traditional desktop virtualization impossible on mobile hardware. Henge completely bypasses this limitation by implementing a proprietary user-space execution pipeline that lets you download, install, and run official macOS arm64 restore images directly on mobile silicon without an intermediary Mac.

🚀 Key Features:
• Custom JIT & Device Emulation: Runs Mac arm64 code via a custom JIT engine with its own Memory Management Unit and device emulation layers.
• Metal-Accelerated Graphics: Intercepts and replays macOS graphics commands using Apple Metal, letting heavy software like Safari, VS Code, and Electron apps render seamlessly.
• Hardware & Peripheral Integration: Automatically detects external displays via USB-C or HDMI docks, maps touchscreens to trackpads, and integrates physical Bluetooth or Magic Keyboards.
• Direct Restore Images: Executes authentic restoration procedures straight from official Apple restore images on mobile hardware.

Whether you are a mobile systems engineer, iOS low-level developer, or security researcher pushing the boundaries of what is possible on locked-down silicon, Henge is an extraordinary reference for user-space instruction emulation and graphics translation.

👉 Check out the source code and dive into the architecture on GitHub:
https://github.com/Leviidev/Henge

Ever wonder what happens to all that unallocated memory sitting on your dev rig? 

Introducing ram-altman: the ultimate bash script that monitors your PC's unused RAM and automatically emails your daily surplus directly to Sam Altman. Blending satirical sysadmin tooling with razor-sharp industry commentary, this is the utility your setup didn't know it needed. 🤖💾

The Problem:
Most simple monitoring tools trigger false positives by ignoring how Linux handles page caches. Calculating true available system memory requires parsing deep kernel metrics without getting tripped up by reclaimable cache.

How It Solves It:
This tool parses Linux kernel memory metrics directly from /proc/meminfo to calculate true available RAM. It tracks historical trends in a local CSV log and uses a cron job to dispatch a humorous daily report whenever your available capacity crosses a configured threshold.

Notable Features:
- Precise Linux memory accounting that correctly handles MemAvailable versus page caches to prevent false positives.
- Built-in state management and strict rate limiting guaranteeing at most one email per day, complete with dry-run preview capabilities.
- Templated email generation that dynamically rotates through multiple subject lines, witty body messages, and sign-offs.
- A comprehensive test suite utilizing simulated memory stats and a mock sendmail binary to ensure zero accidental live mailings.

Developer Value:
While framed as a hilarious parody, the codebase delivers clean, idiomatic Bash scripting patterns. It is an exceptional reference for parsing system metrics, handling state files safely, implementing robust cron-based rate limiting, and structuring automated testing frameworks for shell scripts.

Check it out on GitHub:
https://github.com/IainKay/ram-altman
